message.content: In lions, one of the most well‑known dominant genetic traits is the presence of a mane in males. The gene responsible for mane development is expressed dominantly, meaning that a single copy of the allele is sufficient for a male lion to grow a mane. This trait is not present in females, who typically lack a mane.
